content:
The Mensuration (3-D) chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Mensuration (3-D) tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Mensuration (3-D)

Surface area and volume of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres, and combinations of solids.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Cube: V = a³, TSA = 6a²; Cuboid: V = lbh, TSA = 2(lb+bh+hl).
  • Cylinder: V = πr²h, TSA = 2πr(r+h).
  • Cone: V = ⅓πr²h, slant l = √(r²+h²).
  • Sphere: V = 4⁄3 πr³, SA = 4πr².

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing curved surface area with total surface area.
  • Forgetting the slant height in cone formulas.
  • Unit slips between cm² and cm³.

faq.q: What is the volume of a sphere?
faq.a: 4⁄3 πr³, and its surface area is 4πr².

faq.q: How is a cone’s slant height found?
faq.a: l = √(r² + h²), where r is the base radius and h the vertical height.
